Most tools recommend what is best on average; our user needs to know what happens in the worst year. The farmer taps a field on a satellite map and describes the farm. Every plan explains why it was suggested, the evidence, the benefits, the data gaps and the risks to check in the field. The goal is not a score to trust blindly, but a record to inspect and a plan to try on a small part of the field first.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

NongbuImo ("Farmer Auntie") offers crop-rotation choices to farmers who cannot afford a single failed harvest. The farmer taps a field on a satellite map and describes the farm (last crop, irrigation, slope, soil, priorities). The app loads NASA POWER climate data for that exact point, builds six rotation strategies including the farmer's current practice as a baseline, and replays each one on 34 years of NASA monthly weather (1991-2024). Each plan is reported as "held in N of 34 years", with the worst year named.

HOW IT WORKS

- Rule-based scoring, not machine learning, so every number can be explained: soil health, water balance, pest safety, income and climate fit.

- A 10-day crop calendar, so real double cropping (for example rice then barley) is handled correctly.

- 34-year replay: a year counts as "held" only if every crop in the rotation gets enough water and stays within its temperature tolerance.

- Each plan states why it was suggested, the evidence, the benefits, the data gaps and the risks to check in the field.

- A simulator lets farmers test their own rotation against ours on the same 34 years and share the result with the community.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Rotation can protect soil and reduce fertilizer use, but the farmers who need it most are the least able to risk trying it. We aim to lower that risk: show the worst year before the average, offer options instead of orders, and suggest trying one tenth of the field first so the possible loss is known in advance. The intended impact is fewer catastrophic years for smallholders, and more farmers willing to try a better rotation.

HOW IT IS CREATIVE

Most tools ask the farmer to trust a score. We ask the farmer to inspect a record, and we let them try to prove us wrong. The recommendation is kept independent of the seed market, and the app openly lists what its data cannot see.

WHAT WE CONSIDERED

- Trust: a correct recommendation is useless if the farmer never tries it.

- Honesty about limits: crop water, temperature and income values are estimates that still need verified agronomic sources; monthly data cannot see a storm inside a month, pests or market prices; community posts are demo data stored in the browser.

- Access: one HTML file with no server, so it opens on any phone browser.

TOOLS

HTML, CSS, vanilla JavaScript, Leaflet. Data: NASA POWER API, NASA GIBS (VIIRS, MODIS NDVI, SMAP, GPM IMERG, MODIS LST), ORNL DAAC MODIS subsets, ISRIC SoilGrids, Open-Meteo, Esri World Imagery. Claude (Anthropic) assisted with code and drafting.

This is an independent project, not a NASA product. No NASA endorsement is implied.
